who: Historian of modern English social history at the University of New Mexico; PhD University of London, 1968.

evidence.says: Joined UNM in 1968, was permanently appointed in 1969 and became history department chair in 1980; authored The Making of Modern English Society from 1850.
Authority for Janet Roebuck cites The making of modern English society (1982).
Identifies the author of The Making of Modern English Society from 1850 as Janet Roebuck, Department of History, University of New Mexico.

notes: Institution, period, field and the authority-record work agree.

who: Daniel M. Siegel, historian of physics at Wisconsin–Madison; PhD physics, Berkeley, 1968.

evidence.says: Lists Daniel M. Siegel as emeritus professor, with a Berkeley physics PhD (1968), and author of Innovation in Maxwell’s Electromagnetic Theory.
The April 1978 History of Science Society newsletter identifies Professor Daniel M. Siegel at the University of Wisconsin at Madison.
Authority for Daniel M. Siegel cites Innovation in Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory (1991), identifying its author with the University of Wisconsin.

notes: The Wisconsin historian matches the AHA Berkeley doctorate and supervision period; the matching candidate is n90662643.

who: Valerie Jean Conner, historian at Florida State University and author of The National War Labor Board.

evidence.says: FSU’s history department identifies Valerie Jean Conner as Professor Emerita of History.
FSU Faculty Senate papers dated February 1994 list Valerie Conner among Arts and Sciences faculty nominees.
Authority for Valerie Jean Conner cites her The National War Labor Board, 1918–1919 (1983).

notes: The fuller faculty name, university and period agree with the supervisor; LC identifies the historian’s work.

who: Historian of Roman antiquity and environmental history at Université Laval, appointed in 1981.

evidence.says: Roman historian Ella Hermon joined Laval in 1981, retired in 2011 and continued as an associated professor; supervised doctoral theses.
Lists Ella Hermon as co-supervisor of Maria del Mar Castro Garcia’s 2016 doctorate on water management in Roman Hispania Ulterior-Baetica, matching the AHA student and title.
Authority for Ella Hermon cites Rome et la Gaule Cisalpine avant César (125–59 av. J.-C.), a work on Roman history.

notes: Exact name, Roman-history field, Laval career and a listed student establish the match.

who: Edward Webb Keane, anthropologist at Michigan from 1997; PhD anthropology, Chicago, 1990.

evidence.says: Identifies Edward Webb Keane, Jr., his Chicago anthropology PhD (1990), and Michigan appointment in 1997.
Names Webb Keane as advisor to Daniel Birchok and Andrew Conroe, with the same dissertation titles as the AHA entries.
Webb Keane’s authority cites Signs of recognition and identifies the Michigan anthropologist with a Chicago PhD; this authority is absent from the candidate list.
The supplied Edward Keane authority instead cites King’s Inn admission papers 1607–1867 (1982).
The other supplied Edward Keane authority concerns film acting, including credits for Stolen heaven (1931).

notes: The supplied candidates are other E. Keanes. The supervisor has a separate authority, n96036270, which is not an eligible candidate.

who: Historian of premodern Russia and Eastern Europe, Ohio State then Kansas; PhD Indiana, 1983.

evidence.says: Kansas identifies Eve Levin as history professor emerita, specializing in premodern Russia and Eastern Europe, with an Indiana PhD (1983).
The 2021 award account names her Indiana dissertation, The Role and Status of Women in Medieval Novgorod, and records her move from Ohio State to Kansas in 2003.
Authority for Eve Levin cites The role and status of women in medieval Novgorod (1983).

notes: Dissertation and doctorate agree; the Ohio State-to-Kansas career explains both institutions in the student list.

who: Historian of Darwin and science at Drew University; retired as Oxnam Professor of Science and Society in 2005.

evidence.says: The 2009 interview identifies the Darwin scholar who retired from Drew in 2005 and describes his editorial work on Darwin’s correspondence and notebooks.
Identifies David Kohn as Drew history professor emeritus and editor-in-chief of the Darwin Digital Library of Evolution, with contributions to the Darwin Correspondence Project.
Authority for David Kohn cites A Calendar of the correspondence of Charles Darwin, 1821–1882 (1983).

notes: Drew affiliation, history-of-science field and Darwin correspondence work identify n83065867 among the same-name candidates.

who: Brooke L. Blower, historian of modern America at Boston University; PhD history, Princeton, 2005.

evidence.says: Identifies the BU historian, her arrival in 2006 and her Princeton history doctorate.
Names Brooke Blower as major advisor to Jeanna Kinnebrew (2023), Andrew Bell (2020), Aaron Hiltner (2018) and Zach Fredman (2016).
Authority for Brooke L. Blower cites The Paris of Americans (2005), with usage Brooke Lindy Blower and information from Princeton University Archives.

notes: Name, Princeton doctorate, BU appointment and four students agree. BU’s current list names Arianne Chernock as Elizabeth Grumer’s major advisor; this does not affect Blower’s identity match.
